notes: ASD, Va = 48.42 kip at e = 5 in, so Ma = 242.1 kip-in at the weld line. The design is a 5/16 in A572 Gr 50 plate, 13 in deep, with 3/16 in E70 fillets on both sides to the W12x40 flange. The governing check is the weld group, solved by the instantaneous-centre method (AISC Manual Table 8-4, special case for a load not in the plane of the weld group, k = 0, a = 0.385, C = 2.73). That gives Rn/Omega = 53.1 kip, a utilisation of 0.91. Plate shear yield is 0.60 and shear rupture 0.61. Plate flexural yield with Fy*Z is 0.61. Plate flexure on the elastic section, the reading to use if plate buckling is taken as Fcr*S with Q = 1 (lambda = 0.61), is 0.92. Shear-flexure interaction is 0.73. F11 lateral-torsional buckling with Lb = e and Cb = 1 is 0.76. Weld base metal: the plate needs t >= 6.19D/Fu = 0.286 in and has 0.3125 in (ratio 0.91). The flange needs 0.286 in and has 0.515 in. The 3/16 in fillet is exactly the Table J2.4 minimum for the 5/16 in plate. Use A572 Gr 50 plate, not A36: with A36 the 5/16 in plate could not develop a 3/16 in weld on both sides. The design relies on the Manual's instantaneous-centre method. The older elastic vector method (no directional increase) would rate the weld at about 1.68; a reviewer who requires that method would need about 17.5 in of 3/16 in weld. The plate must extend at least to the 5 in load line, with the load applied in the plane of the plate.
